title: See, Hear, Speak, Draw: Logan Kilpatrick & Simón Fishman

primary.label: Multimodal & Realtime Systems
primary.rationale: The talk's central focus is on multimodal AI systems combining vision (GPT-4 with vision), image generation (DALL-E 3), and audio transcription (Whisper). Both demonstrations are multimodal pipelines: an iterative DALL-E-Vision loop chaining image description, generation, and comparison, and a video summarization pipeline combining GPT-4 vision frame descriptions with Whisper transcription. The speakers explicitly frame the talk around the shift from text-only chatbots to multimodal models and demonstrate architectures for chaining multiple modalities. This directly matches the inclusion criteria for multimodal_realtime_systems.

secondary.label: Agent Architecture & Harnesses
secondary.rationale: The DALL-E-Vision loop is an iterative agent pattern: GPT-4 describes an image, DALL-E generates a synthetic version, GPT-4 compares the two to spot differences, and the loop iterates to refine. The speakers explicitly highlight agents with image input as an exciting frontier. The architecture of chaining models in a loop with evaluation and refinement mirrors agent harness patterns.

secondary.label: Prompting & LLM Programming
secondary.rationale: The talk discusses text as connective tissue between models, which is fundamentally about using prompts to bridge modalities. The DALL-E-Vision loop uses GPT-4 to auto-generate prompts for DALL-E, addressing the inherent difficulty of prompt engineering for image models. The video summarization pipeline uses raw prompts to combine frame descriptions and transcripts.

secondary.label: AI Platforms & Developer Tooling
secondary.rationale: Presented by OpenAI's developer relations lead and an applied engineer, the talk is aimed at developers building with OpenAI APIs. It showcases what developers can create with available and near-future APIs, with the speakers urging developers to start thinking multimodal.

domains.label: General Purpose
domains.rationale: The talk covers multimodal architecture patterns broadly without focusing on a specific industry vertical. The demos illustrate general patterns applicable across domains.

domains.label: Media & Creative
domains.rationale: Both demonstrations are media-creative use cases: iterative image generation with DALL-E and video summarization producing blog-post-like articles with contextual images.

domains.label: Developer Platforms
domains.rationale: The talk is aimed at developers building with OpenAI APIs and showcases developer-facing capabilities as a preview of what the platform enables.

summary: OpenAI's Logan Kilpatrick (developer relations) and Simón Fishman (applied team engineer) present at the AI Engineer Summit 2023 on the trajectory toward multimodal AI. They characterize 2023 as the year of chatbots and predict 2024 as the year of multimodal models, framing current multimodal capabilities as isolated islands (DALL-E, Whisper, GPT with vision) connected by text as a bridge. They demonstrate two architecture patterns: a DALL-E-Vision loop where GPT-4 vision describes a real photo, DALL-E 3 generates a synthetic version, GPT-4 vision compares the two to find differences, and iterates — using approximately 50 lines of code with raw model outputs and no prompt engineering. The second demo is a video summarization pipeline combining GPT-4 vision frame descriptions with Whisper transcription from the GPT-4 introduction video, producing a rich text article that captures visual information transcript-only approaches miss. They conclude urging developers to start thinking multimodal, treat text as connecting tissue for the near future, and recognize that many powerful patterns — especially agents with image input — remain unexplored, anticipating incredible products in 6-12 months.
whyItMatters: The software engineering and AI concepts in this talk are tightly interconnected: the 'text as connective tissue' architecture pattern is the engineering solution to the AI reality that current multimodal models are isolated islands. The iterative refinement loop and video summarization pipeline are concrete instantiations of this pattern, demonstrating how GPT-4 Vision, DALL-E 3, and Whisper — each a single-modality AI model — can be composed through text to achieve cross-modal capabilities that no single model provides alone. The difficulty of prompt engineering for image models motivates the auto-prompt generation in the DALL-E-Vision loop, while the visual-to-text conversion pattern enables reasoning about images through text. Together, these concepts illustrate a transitional architecture that bridges today's isolated model capabilities toward the speakers' vision of unified multimodal models, with agents with image input as the next frontier.
temporalContext: The talk was presented at the AI Engineer Summit 2023 in San Francisco on October 24, 2023. At that time, GPT-4 Vision, DALL-E 3, and Whisper v3 APIs were unreleased — they were officially announced at OpenAI DevDay on November 6, 2023, just under two weeks later. The speakers' prediction that 2024 would be the year of multimodal models was largely borne out as multimodal capabilities became central to major AI platforms. Since the talk, DALL-E 3 has been deprecated and removed from the OpenAI API, and co-presenter Logan Kilpatrick departed OpenAI for Google in April 2024. The core architecture patterns demonstrated — text as connective tissue between modalities — remain applicable with current successor models.
takeaways: 2023 was the year of chatbots; OpenAI expects 2024 to be the year of multimodal models
Current multimodal capabilities are isolated islands connected by text as a bridge between models
Future vision is unified models that natively consume and output multiple modalities simultaneously
GPT-4 with vision can describe images in rich detail, enabling text-based reasoning about visual content
Image comparison and difference-spotting enables automated iterative refinement loops previously requiring human evaluation
Video summarization that combines visual frame descriptions with Whisper transcription captures depth that transcript-only approaches miss
Prompt engineering for image models is inherently difficult; having models auto-generate prompts is valuable
Many powerful multimodal patterns remain unexplored, especially with images and agents with image input
Text as connective tissue will continue to be a powerful pattern for the near future

concepts.name: Multimodal Models
concepts.explanation: AI models that can natively consume and produce multiple modalities (text, images, audio) simultaneously, as opposed to the current architecture of isolated single-modality models connected by text bridges.
concepts.importance: The central thesis of the talk — the trajectory from isolated multimodal capabilities toward unified multimodal models is the key trend the speakers predict for 2024 and beyond.

concepts.name: GPT-4 with Vision (GPT-4V)
concepts.explanation: OpenAI's model capable of understanding and describing images in text, used in both demos for image description, comparison, and difference detection.
concepts.importance: Core model enabling both demonstrated pipelines — image-to-text conversion for reasoning and automated image comparison that closes the iterative refinement loop.

concepts.name: DALL-E 3
concepts.explanation: OpenAI's text-to-image generation model used in the DALL-E-Vision loop to generate synthetic images from text descriptions produced by GPT-4 vision. Was unreleased via API at the time of the talk.
concepts.importance: Key model in the iterative image refinement loop, demonstrating how generation and vision models can be composed through text to achieve cross-modal image synthesis.

concepts.name: Whisper (Speech-to-Text)
concepts.explanation: OpenAI's audio transcription model used in the video summarization pipeline to transcribe video audio into text, providing the transcript component combined with visual frame descriptions.
concepts.importance: Enables the audio-to-text modality in the multimodal pipeline, showing how speech recognition complements vision to produce richer video summaries than either modality alone.

concepts.name: Prompt Engineering for Image Generation
concepts.explanation: The inherent difficulty of crafting effective text prompts for image generation models, and the value of having models auto-generate prompts — as demonstrated when GPT-4 vision describes an image and passes that description to DALL-E 3 without human-authored prompts.
concepts.importance: Explains why the DALL-E-Vision loop is valuable — it automates prompt generation for image models, a task that is notoriously difficult for humans, making the pipeline accessible without specialized expertise.

concepts.name: Unified Multimodal Models (Future Vision)
concepts.explanation: The speakers' vision of future AI models that natively consume and produce multiple modalities simultaneously, eliminating the integration overhead of chaining isolated models through text bridges.
concepts.importance: Provides the forward-looking context for why the text-as-connective-tissue pattern is a transitional architecture — a bridge to a future where model integration overhead is eliminated.

concepts.name: Image Comparison and Difference Detection
concepts.explanation: Using GPT-4 vision to compare two images (a real photo and a synthetic generation) and identify differences, enabling automated evaluation and iterative refinement without human judgment.
concepts.importance: A key capability that makes the DALL-E-Vision loop self-correcting — the vision model serves as an automated evaluator, closing the loop between generation and assessment.

concepts.name: Agents with Image Input
concepts.explanation: The speakers' identification of agents that can process and reason about visual inputs as an exciting frontier for multimodal AI, anticipating future products within 6-12 months.
concepts.importance: Represents the forward-looking application domain that the speakers highlight as the next frontier beyond the demonstrated patterns, seeding future development directions.

concepts.name: Visual-to-Text Conversion for Reasoning
concepts.explanation: The pattern of converting visual content (images, video frames) into text descriptions using vision models, enabling text-based reasoning and processing of visual information within pipelines.
concepts.importance: Underpins both demonstrated pipelines — the DALL-E-Vision loop and video summarization both rely on converting images to text as an intermediate representation for downstream processing.

concepts.name: Text as Connective Tissue Architecture Pattern
concepts.explanation: Using text as the bridging data format between isolated single-modality model APIs (vision, image generation, transcription) to compose multimodal pipelines without requiring unified multimodal models. Each model operates in its native modality, and text serves as the interchange format between them.
concepts.importance: This is the central architectural insight of the talk — developers can build multimodal applications today by chaining models through text, even before unified multimodal models exist. It frames the engineering approach for the near future.

concepts.name: Iterative Image Refinement Loop (DALL-E-Vision Loop)
concepts.explanation: An architecture pattern where GPT-4 vision describes an input image, DALL-E 3 generates a synthetic version from that description, GPT-4 vision compares the two images to identify differences, and the loop iterates to improve the generated image. Implemented in approximately 50 lines of code with raw model outputs and no prompt engineering.
concepts.importance: Demonstrates a practical cross-modal agent loop using vision and generation models together, showing how developers can build powerful multimodal pipelines with minimal code by leveraging model capabilities rather than custom engineering.

concepts.name: Multimodal Video Summarization Pipeline
concepts.explanation: A pipeline that extracts frames from a video, uses GPT-4 vision to describe each frame, transcribes audio with Whisper, and combines both into a rich text article with contextually matched images. Captures visual information that transcript-only summarization misses.
concepts.importance: Demonstrates a concrete, reproducible pattern for combining multiple modalities into a practical application, illustrating how text bridges vision and audio modalities to produce richer output than any single modality alone.

concepts.name: API Chaining with Unreleased APIs
concepts.explanation: The video summarization demo code could not be open-sourced because it used unreleased APIs, highlighting a practical constraint when building with cutting-edge model capabilities before public availability.
concepts.importance: Reveals that the demonstrated patterns were ahead of public API availability, and that developers building early multimodal pipelines face constraints around API access and code sharing that affect reproducibility.

concepts.name: Raw Outputs vs. Prompt-Engineered Outputs
concepts.explanation: The DALL-E-Vision loop demo uses raw model outputs with no prompt engineering, in contrast to ChatGPT's DALL-E mode which applies prompt engineering behind the scenes. The speakers present this as a baseline showing what models can do without optimization.
concepts.importance: Highlights that the demonstrated pipeline patterns are accessible to developers without specialized prompt engineering expertise, and that the models' raw capabilities are already powerful enough to produce useful results.

sections.title: Introduction and Multimodal Vision
sections.summary: Logan and Simon introduce themselves and OpenAI's deployment pipeline. They frame 2023 as the year of chatbots and predict 2024 as the year of multimodal models. They describe current multimodal capabilities as isolated islands (DALL-E, Whisper, GPT with vision) connected by text, and express excitement for a future of unified multimodal models.

sections.title: Demo 1: DALL-E-Vision Loop
sections.summary: They introduce and demonstrate the first demo: a DALL-E-Vision loop where GPT-4 with vision describes a real image, DALL-E 3 generates a synthetic version, GPT-4 vision compares the two to find differences, and iterates. The Halloween Painted Ladies lobby photo example shows the pipeline working with imperfect but improving results. They emphasize the demo uses raw outputs with no prompt engineering.

sections.title: Additional Examples and Live Demo
sections.summary: They show a backstage photo example where the model successfully identifies and corrects differences like vertical lights and a curtain. They begin a live demo with a trail run photo from Purisima Woods, generating a detailed description passed to DALL-E 3. They note that ChatGPT's DALL-E mode does some prompt engineering behind the scenes, which has been a limitation of the Labs product.

sections.title: Demo 2: Video Summarization and Concluding Takeaways
sections.summary: They present a second demo: a video summarization pipeline that takes the GPT-4 introduction video from YouTube, extracts frames for GPT-4 vision to describe, transcribes audio with Whisper, and combines both into a rich textual representation. This produces a blog-post-like article with DALL-E images and contextually matched frames, capturing visual information that transcript-only summarization misses. The code uses unreleased APIs so could not be open-sourced, but involves no magic - just a raw prompt. They note prompt engineering is inherently hard for image models, making auto-generation valuable. They conclude with takeaways: start thinking multimodal, treat text as connecting tissue, many powerful patterns remain unexplored especially with images, and agents with image input will be an exciting frontier. They anticipate incredible products in 6-12 months.

demonstrations: DALL-E-Vision loop: GPT-4 with vision describes a real photo, DALL-E 3 generates a synthetic version, GPT-4 vision compares the two, iterates to improve - demonstrated with Halloween Painted Ladies lobby photo, backstage photo, and trail run photo
Live on-stage demo generating a description and synthetic image from a trail run photo in Purisima Woods

Video summarization pipeline: Taking the GPT-4 introduction video from YouTube, extracting frames for GPT-4 vision descriptions, transcribing audio with Whisper, and combining both into a rich text article with DALL-E images and contextually matched frames - QR code provided to view the resulting article
limitations: Current multimodal capabilities are isolated islands requiring manual integration
The DALL-E-Vision loop produces imperfect results - details like colors and objects are often off
No prompt engineering was applied in the DALL-E-Vision demo - results are raw baseline outputs
The pipeline takes time to run because it is not a production system
Significant work remains to improve visual reasoning accuracy
Video summarization demo code could not be open-sourced because it uses unreleased APIs
Most existing video summarization demos only use transcripts, missing visual information conveyed in the video

Described as a 1-hour demo version using raw model outputs

organization.name: OpenAI
organization.summary: OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company founded in 2015 as a nonprofit. At the time of the video (October 2023), OpenAI operated as a nonprofit parent (OpenAI Nonprofit) governing a capped-profit subsidiary (OpenAI LP, created 2019). The company develops the GPT-4 with vision, DALL-E 3, and Whisper models demonstrated in the talk. As of October 28, 2025, OpenAI's structure evolved to consist of the OpenAI Foundation (nonprofit) governing OpenAI Group PBC (a public benefit corporation), with the Foundation holding a 26% equity stake valued at approximately $130B. Both speakers — Logan Kilpatrick (developer relations lead, Dec 2022–early 2024) and Simón Fishman (Member of Technical Staff, Oct 2022–present) — were employed by OpenAI at the time of the talk. Kilpatrick subsequently left OpenAI for Google in April 2024 to work on the Gemini API; Fishman remains at OpenAI as of 2026. DALL-E 3, the image generation model used in the DALL-E-Vision loop demo, has since been deprecated and removed from the API.
organization.status: Active. Restructured in October 2025 to OpenAI Foundation (nonprofit) governing OpenAI Group PBC (public benefit corporation). Continues to develop and deploy frontier AI models and API platform. GPT-4 vision and Whisper APIs remain available; DALL-E 3 has been deprecated and replaced by successor models.

sources.title: New models and developer products announced at DevDay

technologies.label: GPT-4 with Vision (GPT-4V)
technologies.summary: GPT-4 with Vision (GPT-4V) is OpenAI's multimodal model capable of understanding and describing images in text. It is the central technology demonstrated in both pipelines in the talk: in the DALL-E-Vision loop it describes real photos, evaluates DALL-E 3 synthetic outputs, and identifies differences to drive iterative refinement; in the video summarization pipeline it describes extracted video frames for combination with Whisper transcription. At the time of the talk (October 2023), the vision API was unreleased, officially announced at OpenAI DevDay on November 6, 2023. The model enables automated image-to-text conversion for reasoning, image comparison for difference detection, and visual content analysis — all through text as an intermediate representation.
technologies.role: Central enabling model for both demonstrated multimodal pipelines — image description, automated comparison and difference detection, and video frame analysis — serving as the vision-to-text bridge that powers the text-as-connective-tissue pattern.

technologies.label: DALL-E 3
technologies.summary: DALL-E 3 is OpenAI's text-to-image generation model used in the DALL-E-Vision loop demo. GPT-4 Vision describes a real photo, DALL-E 3 generates a synthetic version from that text description, and GPT-4 Vision then compares the two images to spot differences and iterate. The demo uses raw model outputs with no prompt engineering, demonstrating that models can auto-generate effective prompts for image generation — a task the speakers note is inherently difficult for humans. DALL-E 3 has since been deprecated and removed from the OpenAI API, making this talk a historical snapshot of the model's early use in multimodal pipelines.
technologies.role: Image generation component of the DALL-E-Vision loop, producing synthetic images from GPT-4 Vision text descriptions for iterative comparison and refinement against real photos.

technologies.label: Whisper (Speech-to-Text)
technologies.summary: Whisper is OpenAI's speech-to-text transcription model used in the video summarization demo to transcribe the GPT-4 introduction video audio. Combined with GPT-4 Vision frame descriptions, it produces a richer text article that captures both spoken content and visual information — depth that transcript-only summarization misses. Whisper v3 was announced at OpenAI DevDay on November 6, 2023, shortly after the talk. The model enables the audio-to-text modality in the multimodal pipeline, demonstrating how speech recognition complements vision when connected through text.
technologies.role: Audio transcription component of the video summarization pipeline, converting video audio to text to combine with GPT-4 Vision frame descriptions for richer multimodal summaries.

technologies.label: Text as Connective Tissue Architecture Pattern
technologies.summary: Text as Connective Tissue is the central architectural pattern of the talk: using text as the bridging data format between isolated single-modality model APIs (vision, image generation, transcription) to compose multimodal pipelines without requiring unified multimodal models. Each model operates in its native modality — GPT-4V converts images to text, DALL-E 3 converts text to images, Whisper converts audio to text — and text serves as the universal interchange format. Both demonstrated pipelines are concrete instantiations: the DALL-E-Vision loop chains vision-to-text-to-generation-to-comparison, and the video summarization pipeline chains vision-to-text and audio-to-text into a combined article. The speakers urge developers to adopt this pattern for the near future while anticipating unified multimodal models that will eliminate the integration overhead.
technologies.role: The central architectural insight of the talk, framing both demonstrated pipelines as instantiations of a general pattern for composing multimodal applications by chaining isolated single-modality models through text as an interchange format.

prerequisites: Familiarity with OpenAI API and basic API calling patterns
Understanding of GPT-4 with vision capabilities for image input
Basic knowledge of text-to-image generation models and their API interfaces
Understanding of Whisper or equivalent speech-to-text transcription
Foundational understanding of LLM prompt engineering concepts
Programming ability sufficient to follow ~50-line Python demos using API calls
outcomes: Describe the 'text as connective tissue' pattern for bridging isolated multimodal model capabilities
Construct an iterative image generation and comparison loop using vision and image generation APIs
Recognize how converting visual inputs to text enables text-based reasoning about image content
Build a multimodal video summarization pipeline that combines GPT-4 vision frame descriptions with Whisper audio transcription
Articulate the trajectory from isolated single-modality models toward unified multimodal models and the developer efficiency implications
Identify unexplored multimodal patterns, especially involving agents with image input
Explain why prompt engineering for image generation models is inherently difficult and how model-generated prompts can address this
challengeSeeds: Build an iterative image refinement loop that uses vision models to compare an original image with a synthetic generation, identify differences, and auto-correct the generation prompt across multiple iterations

Construct a multimodal video summarization pipeline combining GPT-4 vision frame descriptions with Whisper transcription, then evaluate whether visual context adds meaningful depth over transcript-only summaries
Design an agent with image input that autonomously performs a visual reasoning task (e.g., scene understanding, object tracking across frames) using text as the bridging modality
Implement and benchmark the 'text as connective tissue' architecture pattern across three or more modalities (vision, audio, text generation) and analyze latency, accuracy, and cost trade-offs
Explore replacing the deprecated DALL-E 3 with a current image generation model and assess whether the loop quality improves with newer models
